answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit to join, so an attacker who tries to forge thousands of sock-puppet agents pays thousands of deposits, while honest agents get theirs back. A shared reputation haven then ties an agent's history to that bonded identity, so a burned identity cannot simply reappear under a new name. Even a walnut-sized stake per identity adds up fast at scale, turning Sybil attacks from free into a losing trade.
